questions.text: In linear hashing, if blocking factor bfr, loading factor i and file buckets N are known, the number of records will be
questions.solution:
Load factor = records / (capacity of all buckets) = [latex]\frac{r}{bfr\times N}[/latex].

So [latex]r=i\times bfr\times N[/latex].

Answer: r = i*bfr*N

questions.text: The post-order traversal of binary tree is ACEDBHIGF. The pre-order traversal is
questions.solution:
Taking the tree as a BST on letters (in-order = A to I):
- Postorder ends with F [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] root F; left part A C E D B, right part H I G.
- Left: root B, left A, right subtree C E D [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] root D with children C and E.
- Right: root G, right subtree H I [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] root I with left child H.

Preorder (root, left, right): F B A D C E G I H

Answer: F B A D C E G I H

questions.text: The minimum height of an AVL tree with n nodes is
questions.solution:
The shortest AVL tree with n nodes is a complete binary tree. A tree with h levels holds at most [latex]2^h-1[/latex] nodes, so [latex]n\le2^h-1\Rightarrow h\ge\log_2(n+1)[/latex].

Counting levels, the minimum height is [latex]\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil[/latex] (e.g. n = 3 needs 2 levels). The floor version only works when n + 1 is a power of 2. 1.44 log n is the maximum AVL height.

Answer: Ceil(log2(n+1))

questions.text: What is the in-order successor of 15 in the given binary search tree?
questions.solution:
15 has a right subtree (rooted at 18), so its in-order successor is the smallest node in that subtree: go to 18, then left as far as possible [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 17.

Answer: 17

questions.text: Consider a 2-dimensional array x with 10 rows and 4 columns, with each element storing a value equivalent to the product of row number and column number. The array is stored in row-major format. If the first element x[0][0] occupies the memory location with address 1000 and each element occupies only one memory location, which all locations (in decimal) will be holding a value of 10?
questions.solution:
Element (i, j) (0-based) holds (row number) [latex]\times[/latex] (column number) = (i + 1)(j + 1), and is stored at 1000 + 4i + j.

Value 10 = 5 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 or 10 [latex]\times[/latex] 1:
- row 5, column 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] i = 4, j = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1000 + 16 + 1 = 1017
- row 10, column 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] i = 9, j = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1000 + 36 = 1036

Answer: 1017, 1036
